A Day in the Life: On a cross-functional team, your day is about how the team works together, more than what it builds. You carry out and see through the facilitation: running sprint planning, retrospectives, and demos, helping the team set working agreements and clear roles, tracking sprint progress, and coaching people one on one. You produce things like working agreements, a team process map, a psychological safety plan, and agile maturity measurements. You are consulted across the whole team, since improving how people collaborate touches every function. A typical day mixes facilitation, a standup you keep crisp and a planning or retro session you guide, with one-on-one coaching conversations and light tracking in Notion, FigJam, and Trello. You lead by serving the team rather than directing it, help people work through friction, and nudge the group toward better habits in short, steady loops.
